title: Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol: universal sufficient grace is a slippery postulate — Vasquez grants some infants never received sufficient media of salvation
pass_a_gloss: That postulate concerning sufficient grace prepared and administered unto all is very slippery, and among the patrons of universal grace themselves has not yet been approved by full and firm consent. Vasquez (which we noted before), convicted by the very evidence of the thing, grants that unto certain infants the sufficient media of salvation could neither by any human providence have been applied, nor by Divine providence were applied, In T. Aquin. disp. 95. cap. 6. We can therefore, as to these little ones so perishing in original sin, turn back this reason thus: Those infants unto whom sufficient media were not prepared and administered were rejected without consideration of actual unbelief, or of final impenitence.
pass_b_english: The claim that sufficient grace is prepared and administered to all is very slippery — and even among patrons of universal grace it lacks full firm consent. Vasquez (as we noted before), forced by the plain fact, grants that for some infants sufficient media of salvation could not be applied by any human providence and were not applied by divine providence (In T. Aquin. disp. 95.6). So for these little ones perishing in original sin we can turn their argument back: infants for whom sufficient media were never prepared or administered were rejected without regard to actual unbelief or final impenitence.
source_text: Illud de gratia sufficiente omnibus parata et administrata postulatum valde lubricum est, et inter ipsos gratiae universalis patronos nondum pleno et firmo consensu approbatum. Vasques (quod ante annotavimus) ipsa rei evidentia convictus concedit, quibusdam infantibus sufficientia salutis media neque humana ulla providentia potuisse applicari, neque Divina providentia fuisse applicata, In T. Aquin. disp. 95. cap. 6. Possumus igitur, quoad hosce parvulos in originali peccato sic pereuntes, retorquere hanc rationem hoc modo: Quibus infantibus media sufficientia praeparata et administrata non fuerunt, illi rejecti fuerunt sine consideratione actualis infidelitatis, aut finalis impoenitentiae.
